title: Diagnose missing TRIM signals and restoration opportunity costs
body:
Adds an offline diagnostic study for AMD, NVDA and MU without modifying Risk Engine v2, its thresholds or the existing execution/restoration simulator. This PR targets feature/risk-backtest-v1 and depends on #2; neither #1 nor #2 is merged.

Outputs in reports/risk-diagnostics: daily-signals.csv (111 sessions), drawdown-events.csv (18 deduplicated peak/threshold rows), recovery-analysis.csv (9 extended-period reductions/restorations), report.md, indicator-evaluation.csv and reproducibility/validation metadata. Daily rows include prior-only 20/60/120 drawdowns, MA20/50/200, RSI14, VIX, historical support, relative performance against downloaded QQQ, and every relevant Overlay predicate plus explicit blockers. Retrospective labels remain separate from decision features.

Findings for September 1–October 22, 2026: all 111 decisions are HOLD. Maximum VIX is 19.99 (below stress 25/severe 30), and no stock breaks its prior-120-bar support. Recent drawdowns do not enter the current TRIM formula. Worst DD20 is AMD -21.79%, NVDA -11.30%, MU -21.95%; no first REVIEW/TRIM occurs for these three stocks. Missing historical regime/breadth are not fabricated. With no support break, a defensive regime alone could add REVIEW, but not activate the conjunctive TRIM branch.

Extended recoveries occur after August 2024, April 2025 and March 2026 reductions, with 5/19/5 sessions of reduced exposure. Returning to full invested weight at higher prices can buy fewer shares. The new FIFO decomposition exactly reconciles prior missed-recovery metrics: AMD $1,497.37, NVDA $2,658.67, MU $5,631.35 per initially $10,000 independent account. Matched repurchase costs and terminal residual-share marking are separated from the simpler first-restoration price gap and from actual return differences. None of these diagnostics alone proves that an earlier return would have been superior.

Fixed alternative indicators (fall acceleration, local drawdown, MA crossings, relative QQQ weakness, rising VIX) are examined on separate pre-window and requested-period samples. All active/inactive counts, missing inputs and censored horizons are reported. No October-specific optimization or production rule changes. Candidate restoration policies are discussed for later walk-forward testing, not presented as validated improvements.

Validation: 77 tests passed, 20 subtests passed; no failing/skipped tests. Includes future-price/publication exclusion, numerical threshold boundaries, episode deduplication/nested MU drawdown, missing-indicator handling, exact agreement with the prior replay, three-HOLD restoration and FIFO reconciliation. Engine/simulator hashes, compilation, output hashes and staged whitespace checks passed.

Limitations: this remains the PR #2 price/VIX-only replay on retrospective provider vintages with inferred publication times, not a fully verified point-in-time Alpha OS reconstruction. QQQ adds relative-price context, not historical breadth. Forward-outcome rates are descriptive, overlapping and often censored in late October. Signal absence is distinguished from proven decision inefficiency. No Railway, PostgreSQL, production service changes, deployments or merges.
head: research/risk-signal-diagnostics
